subject: Virtual identical latent variables can't be merged/fixed to 1?

messages.author: 19f064f2ba314361
messages.subject: Virtual identical latent variables can't be merged/fixed to 1?
parts:
Hey all

In my following model I apply fixed-links modelling in order to dissociate different sources of variance within two elementary cognitive tasks (ECTs).
For each ECT, I model a constant process (processes common to all task levels, not changing across levels, e.g. basal speed processes) and a variable process (processes increasing across task levels, e.g. increasing complexity).

I specify the following model according to my theoretical assumptions:
hick = variable with increasing complexity (factor loadings fixed to 1, 2, and 4)
cHICK = constant variable (factor loadings fixed to 1)
similar fixing for cpt
+ restraints by setting covariances to 0 in order to assume independent latent variables

modelA      <- 'hick   =~ 1*hick_rt1m   + 2*hick_rt2m   + 4*hick_rt3m
                  cHICK =~ 1*hick_rt1m   + 1*hick_rt2m   + 1*hick_rt3m
                  cCPT =~  1*cpt_rt1m + 1*cpt_rt2m + 1*cpt_rt3m
                  cpt =~ 0.25*cpt_rt1m + 2*cpt_rt2m + 3*cpt_rt3m
                  hick ~~ cpt
                  hick ~~ 0*cHICK
                  cpt ~~ 0*cCPT
                  hick ~~ 0*cCPT
                  cpt ~~ 0*cHICK
                  cHICK ~~ cCPT'

This model fits well / good indices (p = .31) -> graph on the left
due to the standardized coefficients I can assume that the two constant processes represent virtual identical processes (cHICK and cCPT = .975). Anyhow, when I model the same model with the two constant variables as one variable (-> graph on the right), then the model won't fit anymore (p = .004) and show rather poor indices.
(Modindices tell me that the (new) constant variable should be covaried with hick...)

can anyone tell me, from a methodological perspective, why it works for the two contant model and why it doesn't work at all for the one constant model?
To my understanding, the model on the right is more parsimonious and should be better than the model on the left...

messages.author: bfa43814f6ba1969
messages.subject: Re: Virtual identical latent variables can't be merged/fixed to 1?
parts:
Hi

Note that by constraining two latent variables to be the same you are not constraining their correlation to be 1, but also their scales to be the same. You are reporting standardized estimates. If you look at the raw estimates and the estimated variances of cHICK and cCPT, you are likely to find what the problem is.

Mikko
